subject: Overnight P2 coverage exception request - BrightRiver Analytics
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@brightriver.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.soto@brightriver.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Overnight P2 coverage during planned migration - exception request

Hi Logan,

Quick background: BrightRiver is doing a data plane migration the night of Sep 26–27. We expect a higher-than-normal rate of alerts as we cut over a small set of tenants. Our security team requires on-call continuity for P1s, but product leadership is asking if we can request a temporary carve-out for P2s overnight to avoid unnecessary wake-ups while we validate.

Can Redwood accept a temporary P2 overnight response window (i.e., move P2 to next-business-hour handling for one night), with the following guardrails:
- Redwood provides a 1-hour triage visible in the console and a follow-up ticket the next morning.
- For any P1s or customer-impacting incidents, normal P1 on-call escalation still applies.
- We (BrightRiver) will provide the maintenance plan and a Slack channel monitored by our ops team.

Attached is our migration runbook and the list of affected tenant IDs. Please advise who we should loop in on your side for a formal exception and if there's any credit or SLA impact.

Thanks,
Chris Nolan
Head of Platform Ops
BrightRiver Analytics

Attachments: brightriver-maintenance-plan-2027-09.pdf
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@brightriver.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight P2 coverage during planned migration - exception request

Chris —

Thanks for the heads up and the runbook. We can support a temporary P2 carve-out for that window under a controlled exception, provided the conditions are explicit (which they largely are). A few clarifying points before I escalate for approval:

1) Duration: confirm start/end UTC timestamps for the carve-out (we need exact window).
2) Scope: confirm tenant IDs and whether any regulated tenants are in scope.
3) Communication: we need a dedicated incident Slack channel and an on-call BrightRiver point of contact for the night.
4) Escalation path: we will not change P1 handling — P1s still follow our standard on-call. For P2s we can switch to next-business-day handling but Redwood duty engineer will perform a 1-hour automated triage and annotate the ticket.

On our side: Laura (Head of CS Ops) and Marissa (Service Reliability lead) are on this thread — they'll help draft the exception and the minimal SLO amendment for the night.

Two quick asks:
- Laura/Marissa, can you draft the exception notice and include the fallback escalation (phone numbers) we will use if the incident escalates to P1?
- Chris, can BrightRiver confirm the exact UTC window and whether any PCI/PHI customers are affected? If regulated, we may need approval from security which takes ~24 hours.

Logan Wright
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@brightriver.com>, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight P2 coverage during planned migration - exception request

Chris, Logan —

I've sketched a minimal exception the Support team can sign off on. Key bullets below (I attached a spreadsheet with proposed handoff rotations):

- Exception window: 2027-09-26 02:00 UTC to 2027-09-27 06:00 UTC.
- Scope: tenant IDs listed in the runbook; no PCI/PHI-tagged tenants included (BrightRiver confirmed this by email earlier).
- Triage: automated alerting & 1-hour duty-engineer check; duty-engineer must post an incident note in the ticket within 60 minutes.
- P1s: immediate page to on-call as usual, follow P1 runbook (phone + SMS escalation ladder).
- P2s during window: recorded and routed to next-business-hour queue (Redwood SLA credit not applicable for transient carve-outs <48 hours).
- Fallback: If more than 3 distinct P2s are raised within the window and any show signs of customer impact, Redwood will cancel the carve-out and revert to standard P2 handling.

Escalation contacts (Redwood):
- Primary duty engineer (night): +1 415-555-0124 (Marissa Cole)
- On-call manager (day): +1 650-555-0188 (Laura Bennett)
- Sales escalation (if contract/credits discussion): Logan Wright +1 415-555-0101

Marissa, can you confirm availability to be on rotation for that night or propose a shadow?

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-handoff-rotations.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@brightriver.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight P2 coverage during planned migration - exception request

All —

I'm available to provide the duty-engineer rotation and will take the primary overnight slot for 26–27 Sep. Confirmed next steps:

1) BrightRiver: please share the final runbook and a single Slack channel (add marissa.cole@redwood.ai). We'll join the channel 30 minutes before your start window.
2) BrightRiver: confirm the UTC window in writing; we'll add the exception to the service record and route alerts accordingly.
3) Redwood: we'll create a temporary SLO amendment document and email it for signature (no credit applied for single-night carve-outs unless threshold triggers).

If anything materially changes (scope increase, regulated tenant included), we will revert immediately and page the full on-call.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Service Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0124
